value.reason: server.ts:306 exposes the 'logs' directory at /support/logs using serveIndex. The only middleware in front of it is serveIndexMiddleware, and nothing in the Evidence shows an authentication or authorization check like security.isAuthorized(). The line is also tagged as the accessLogDisclosureChallenge vulnerable line. The same directory receives the morgan 'combined' access log (server.ts:362-370), and that format records the full request URL, including the query string. routes/changePassword.ts:14-17 assigns secrets from the request query (redacted in the Evidence, but they look like the current and new password values), and routes/securityQuestion.ts reads the email from query parameters. So passwords and email addresses sent in URLs get written to logs/access.log.*, and anyone who can reach the unauthenticated /support/logs directory can list and read those files. This matches the positive example (an unprotected serveIndex directory holding personal or authentication data) and not the negative one, which adds an isAuthorized() guard. Access control over this resource is missing.
